summary: iter199 RETEST after the phases[iterations] → phases[].duration migration. ALL 16/16 pytest cases pass, including the two iter198 blockers (schedule-downgrade + cancel-scheduled-change) and TWO new iter199 tests (full family→solo downgrade+cancel cycle for a FRESH familydg+<ts>@example.com user with real Stripe test-mode subscription, plus orphan-schedule safety check). Verified against live Stripe test mode: SubscriptionSchedule is created with 2 phases, phase 0 normalizes `duration:{day,14}` into concrete start_date/end_date exactly 14 days apart (1,209,600s), end_behavior=release. GET /api/billing/subscription correctly shows plan=family + pending_plan=solo + pending_effective + non-null current_period_end during pending, and clears after cancel-scheduled-change releases the Stripe schedule. Duplicate-plan downgrade (family → family) is rejected 400 BEFORE any schedule is created — no orphan.

minor.issue: Two extra Stripe round-trips needed to fix the basil 2025-08-27 breakage: (a) `iterations` param removed → replaced with `duration:{interval,interval_count}` read from the current price's recurring config; (b) Stripe additionally requires `start_date` on phase 0 whenever `duration` is used on `modify` (otherwise Stripe returns 'missing start_date to anchor end dates to'). Backend now passes `start_date=_sub_period_start(sub)` on phase 0. Full fix in /app/backend/routes/payments.py:572-604.
Rate-limit buckets rl:signup_ip / rl:signup_email in Redis still block rapid pytest reruns (~5 hits then 7-min lockout). Cleared via flush before each run in this iteration.

rca of the issue: Root cause of the iter198 failure was Stripe API version basil (2025-08-27) removing `phases[].iterations`. iter198 fix attempted `duration:{day,14}` but hit a SECOND undocumented-in-changelog constraint: `duration` on a `SubscriptionSchedule.modify` call requires phase 0 to also carry `start_date` (Stripe error: 'missing start_date to anchor end dates to'). iter199 fix in payments.py:572-604 adds `start_date=_sub_period_start(sub)` on phase 0 and reads `duration` from `current_price.recurring` (day/14 for Wayly's fortnightly billing), which Stripe accepts and normalizes to concrete start_date/end_date 14 days apart. Verified live against Stripe test mode.
